conviction_note: Two forces of similar size pull against each other. The European 2026 crop is a guidance risk the company has not quantified (NEPG -24/25%, worse since the July call per Stephens). Against it, Q1 sits inside an explicit company guide (EBITDA down low teens), and the stock is washed out (-24% in September, -34% from high, put/call 2.56 against a 1.22 average) going into a print where a reaffirmed FY guide would surprise the puts. Findings sum to -0.4; the scaled number is 9.5 x (2 x 0.49 - 1) = -0.19. Both are near zero because the evidence offsets, not because the move will be small.
bar: Q1 FY27 consensus EPS $0.59 (vs $0.74 a year ago) on revenue $1.65-1.66B, from two agreeing sources: potatoes.news 2026-09-30 (https://potatoes.news/us-lamb-weston-to-report-first-quarter-results-on-october-6-as-analysts-expect-eps-to-fall-to-0-59/) and Investing.com (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/lamb-weston-earnings-up-next-can-it-repeat-last-quarters-beat-93CH-4932357). Company guide: Q1 adj EBITDA down 'low teens' from $302.2M (implies about $260-268M) per the Q4 FY26 call (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-lamb-weston-tops-q4-2026-estimates-as-volume-rises-93CH-4812068); FY27 adj EBITDA $1.1-1.2B, EPS $2.95-3.25, sales +0-1% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001679273/000167927326000024/a-lwx20260531xexx991fy26v2.htm). FY consensus EPS about $3.02, below the guide midpoint of $3.10 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/lamb-weston-nyselw-issues-fy-2027-earnings-guidance-2026-07-24/). The stock trades on the FY guide.
positioning_check: Short interest 4.6% of shares and 4.8 days to cover at the 2026-08-31 settlement (https://equibles.com/stocks/lw/short-interest); stockanalysis.com on 2026-10-05: 6.66m shares, 4.89% of float, 5.06 days to cover (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/lw/statistics/). Ortex 2026-10-03: 4.73% of free float, up about 15% in a month; borrow 0.51% and very loose; put/call volume 2.56 against a 20-day average of 1.22, near its 52-week high (https://ortex.news/articles/179722/lamb-weston-bears-pile-into-puts-before-tuesday-print). Not a crowded short. Baseline skew_25d is +1.39 vol points, which the baseline reads as 'balanced'. Open-interest put/call is 4.05, partly from a 14,130-lot of Oct-16 $37.50 puts on 2026-09-18, which IV behaviour suggests was sold rather than bought (https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/lamb-weston-options-flow-shows-nearpure-bearish-positioning-at-3750-strike-93CH-4907597). The event-implied move is 8.99%.

findings.finding: The 2026 north-west European potato crop is forecast at about 20.7-20.8m t, down 24-25% on 2025's 27.3m t (NEPG). Yields are 7-21% below the five-year average, about half of Belgium's main processing variety fails buyers' size requirements, and free-buy prices sit at EUR 20-27.50/100kg against 2026 contracts struck 15-25% below last year. Stephens (2026-09-28) says the crop 'worsened materially since' the July call. The company guided International EBITDA +40-50% for FY27 before this deterioration. The risk is a trim to the International guide or to the $1.1-1.2B EBITDA range; the offset is the CFO's own 2026-08-14 view that industry-wide cost pressure is 'a stronger base for price increases' and that LW is 'mostly contracted'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: LW trades on the FY guide: -25.9% on 2025-12-19 and -20.1% on 2024-12-19 (guide cuts), +16.3% on 2025-07-23 and +10.0% on 2025-04-03 (baseline). The July 2026 guide moved it +0.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: JPM ($52 to $46, 2026-09-30) and Stephens ($55 to $50, 2026-09-28) both cut targets on this crop, and the stock fell 24% in September. If the market already held a cut to the International guide, the skew would not be balanced (+1.39) and consensus FY EPS ($3.02) would sit below the guide's low end. It sits at the low-to-mid of the range, so a quantified cost hit is not in estimates.
findings.independence: Same direction from potatoes.news 2026-10-03, contracts vs spot (https://potatoes.news/eu-potato-market-splits-in-two-as-spot-prices-leave-2026-contracts-behind/), and Stephens via Investing.com (https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/stephens-cuts-lamb-weston-stock-price-target-on-europe-concerns-93CH-4919969). The company's own CFO, 2026-08-14, confirmed a heat-challenged crop with lower yields but also 'mostly contracted' and 'stronger base for price increases' (https://www.just-food.com/news/lamb-weston-flags-price-risks-from-heat-impacted-potato-crop/). Net of the rest: North America is about two-thirds of sales and FY26 segment EBITDA was overwhelmingly NA; International Q4 EBITDA was $11.8M.

findings.finding: The North American 2026 crop is smaller but of good quality. Idaho planted 298,915 acres, its smallest crop since 2011, and some growers report yields up to 20% below 2025 after six weeks of 90F+ heat; quality is 'solid' but sizes run small, and the Columbia Basin lost only 'the top end' of yield. This follows a 2025 crop so large that LW wrote off excess potatoes in FY26, and 2026 NA contract prices were guided down low-to-mid single digits in April. The net cost effect on FY27 is ambiguous: less waste and lower contract prices against smaller sizing, which hurts fry recovery.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean prior on a crop-only surprise. The 2025-12-19 -25.9% guide cut was attributed partly to industry supply and utilisation (Q3 FY26 commentary: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/frozen-lamb-weston-beats-earnings-165200833.html).
findings.why_not_priced: Analyst cuts named Europe, not North America. Management said in July that the NA crop was 'off to a strong start' with contracted acreage 'modestly higher', so a smaller Idaho crop is news since the guide. Its sign is unclear, which is why it is small.
findings.independence: Freshplaza, yields down up to 20% (https://www.freshplaza.com/north-america/article/9879009/idaho-potato-yields-fall-up-to-20-due-to-water-shortage/); potatoes.news 2026-09-30 on 'smallest crop since 2011' (https://potatoes.news/us-lamb-weston-to-report-first-quarter-results-on-october-6-as-analysts-expect-eps-to-fall-to-0-59/). These are proxies: the company has not spoken on the NA crop since July.

findings.finding: The company itself guided Q1 FY27 adj EBITDA down 'low teens' from $302.2M (about $260-268M) because of carryover old-crop potato cost and edible-oil inflation, with growth ramping after Q1. Consensus EPS of $0.59 (-20% YoY) on $1.65-1.66B sits on that guide. LW has cleared its bar in recent quarters (Q4 FY26 EPS $0.87 against $0.62-0.63; sales and EBITDA above the top of the FY26 guide), so a modest beat on the quarter is the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name sells or ignores beats: Q3 FY26 (2026-04-01) beat EPS and revenue and fell 8.9%; Q4 FY26 (2026-07-24) beat by about 40% on EPS and moved +0.8% (baseline; https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/frozen-lamb-weston-beats-earnings-165200833.html).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the quarter lands inside what the company told the market. Only the size of the beat is open. Because beats here have not been paid, the finding is small.
findings.independence: The Q4 FY26 8-K exhibit shows the beat record (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001679273/000167927326000024/a-lwx20260531xexx991fy26v2.htm). This shares the company as its source with the bar field.

findings.finding: At the BofA SMID conference on 2026-08-14, three weeks after the guide, the CFO flagged input-cost pressure from the Middle East conflict (oil, polypropylene packaging, soy oil) and freight and packaging costs up 'since February'. He did not say whether this was inside the FY27 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cost-driven guide cuts have produced the name's largest moves (-25.9%, -20.1%), but those were demand and pricing resets, not input-cost items.
findings.why_not_priced: Edible-oil inflation was already named in the July Q1 guide, so much of this sits inside the guide; that is why it is small. What is not priced is any quantification beyond what was guided. If the market held one, FY consensus would sit at the guide's low end.
findings.independence: Shares one document (the 2026-08-14 CFO remarks) with the price-increase offset cited in finding 1. Freshplaza covers the same event (https://www.freshplaza.com/north-america/article/9863554/lamb-weston-flags-european-potato-yield-and-price-risks/).

findings.finding: McDonald's, LW's swing customer, reported US Q2 2026 comps of only +0.8% (against +2.5% a year earlier) with negative guest counts. It said the US business was 'falling short', with traffic problems that 'persisted into July', which overlaps LW's June-August Q1. LW's July call put QSR burger traffic at -4% in its Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Traffic softness was cited in the 2024-12-19 guide cut (-20.1%). FY26 NA volume (+9 to 11%) came from share and contract wins rather than traffic, which weakens the link.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for two months and probably mostly priced. The open question is whether LW's share-gain volume (FY27 guide: low single-digit volume growth) offsets it. If it were fully priced, Q1 revenue consensus would be below flat; it is flat to -0.6%.
findings.independence: Placer.ai via QSRweb (2026-09-14) shows late-August QSR traffic 1.6% above the H1 average and McDonald's +3.0%, which partly offsets (https://www.qsrweb.com/news/restaurant-traffic-moderates-but-qsrs-remain-above-2026-average/). This is a proxy, not an LW number.

findings.finding: Conagra, reporting 2026-09-30 for a quarter ended 2026-08-30 (the same months as LW's Q1), showed Foodservice organic sales +3.3% with volume +2.5%, about 1.5 points of that from order timing, and segment operating profit +11.4%. It reaffirmed its FY guide. This points to US foodservice demand that did not deteriorate over June-August.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history of LW reacting to a Conagra print.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer print after LW last spoke, in a small segment ($273M) that no LW preview cites. The read-across is weak, which is why it is small.
findings.independence: General Mills (2026-09-23) and Darden (2026-09-24) both reaffirmed FY guides for August-ending quarters (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/24/darden-restaurants-dri-q1-2027-earnings.html). This is a proxy.

findings.finding: Positioning is washed out into the print. LW fell 24.2% in September, the worst in consumer staples (GuruFocus 2026-10-01). It is 34% off its 52-week high and 11.9% down over 20 days. Put/call volume ran at 2.56 against a 1.22 average on 2026-10-03, and OI put/call is 4.05. Yet short interest is a modest 4.7-4.9% with loose borrow, and the 25-delta skew is only +1.39. A reaffirmed FY guide with a constructive pricing or contracting update would land against heavy protective put demand.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After a heavy pre-print drawdown into the 2025-07-23 print, the stock rose 16.3% (baseline). The July 2026 beat with an in-line guide moved it only +0.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: Ortex itself reads the put demand as protection against a large move rather than a directional view, so the downside is hedged rather than shorted. A balanced skew alongside a 24% monthly fall says the price has absorbed the crop news rather than the options paying up for more.
findings.independence: GuruFocus, September performance (https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9105329/lamb-weston-holdings-lw-leads-consumer-staples-decline-in-september-2026); Trefis 2026-09-11, eight straight down days with no named catalyst (https://www.trefis.com/stock/lw/articles/615030/lamb-weston-stock-8-straight-red-days-down-14/2026-09-11).

findings.finding: LW bought back about 1.5M shares at $41.04 average ($63.2M) in Q4 FY26 and has $245M of authorisation left. With the stock at about $44 through most of Q1, a continued buyback, disclosed in the release, is likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Buybacks have not visibly moved LW's prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Small and partly in EPS estimates; it shows only in Q1 share count and the disclosure.

baseline_tension: Mixed. The European crop finding agrees with the 20-day -11.9% run-up and the September -24%, so much of it is in the price. The washed-out positioning finding cuts against that run-up. The skew (+1.39) is balanced and does not take a side, so neither sign fights a strong skew.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold its Q3 beat and ignored its Q4 beat): Q1 reported-quarter finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3
Rule 6 (inside what the company guided): Middle East and edible-oil costs cut from -0.5 to -0.3, since the Q1 guide already named edible-oil inflation
Rule 5 (weather and proxy inference ranks below documents): European crop cut from -1.0 to -0.8, NA crop from -0.3 to -0.2, McDonald's traffic from -0.4 to -0.3; none dropped, all still filed
Rule 7 (positioning is the thing to beat): positioning trimmed from +1.0 to +0.8 because the skew is balanced rather than extreme and short interest is modest
